themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints skyrocketed to 3 this week compared to a 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 2300% spike (z-score 8.69)—suggesting a coordinated or sudden surge in unlicensed advertising, graffiti postings, or unauthorized signage across Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 3 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% increase)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically extreme deviation from baseline
Pattern emerged suddenly this week, not gradual trend
reporting_angles: Map where the 3 complaints are concentrated this week—are they clustered in one neighborhood or scattered?
Interview Department of Sanitation about whether they've noticed a coordinated campaign or if this reflects a specific event (concert, protest, election posting season)

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints surged to 20 this week versus a 7.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 186% spike (z-score 5.96)—raising concerns about mold, ventilation failures, or building code violations affecting resident health in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 20 indoor air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.0 weekly average (186% increase, z-score 5.96)
Timing aligns with ongoing heat/hot water complaint volume (4335 over 90 days), suggesting possible connection to building climate control failures
Recent deadly Inwood blaze (May 14) cited landlords for fire escape violations, indicating broader building maintenance neglect
reporting_angles: Interview residents filing complaints about whether issues are tied to landlord negligence, poor ventilation in aging buildings, or external air quality factors
Cross-reference with DOB records: are these complaints coming from buildings with outstanding violations or recent alteration permits?

themes_detail.label: Helicopter Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Helicopter noise complaints jumped to 3 this week from a 0.5 weekly average—a 500% spike (z-score 3.54)—indicating a sudden increase in aerial activity, likely medical helicopters, news helicopters, or NYPD flights over the district.
evidence: 3 helicopter noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% increase, z-score 3.54)
Unexpected deviation suggests event-driven activity rather than baseline pattern
Correlates with elevated safety complaints (27 last week vs. 12.6 avg, +114%)
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD, EMS, and Coast Guard to identify what triggered the helicopter activity this week
Determine if complaints cluster on specific days or times, indicating a one-off incident vs. ongoing operation

themes_detail.label: Safety Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Safety complaints surged to 27 last week versus a 12.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 114% spike (z-score 3.99)—suggesting a recent escalation in crime, street harassment, or public safety concerns across Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 27 safety complaints LAST WEEK vs. 12.6 weekly average (114% increase, z-score 3.99)
Timing follows deadly Inwood blaze coverage (May 14), which cited landlords for fire escape violations
Encampment complaints also elevated: 18 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.1 avg (+336%, z-score 4.21), suggesting potential links to homelessness and street safety
reporting_angles: Request NYPD crime statistics for the past 2 weeks to validate if major crimes or quality-of-life offenses drove the 311 spike
Interview residents and community leaders about whether the spike reflects real incidents or heightened awareness post-fire
Examine if encampment complaints are tied to the safety complaints—are there new homeless encampments appearing?

themes_detail.label: Encampment Expansion
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 18 two weeks ago from a 4.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 336% spike (z-score 4.21)—indicating a surge in street homelessness or makeshift settlements in Washington Heights/Inwood, a persistent community board concern.
evidence: 18 encampment complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 4.1 weekly average (336% increase, z-score 4.21)
Park safety enhancement is a top recurring community board budget request, indicating long-standing concern
Overlaps with safety complaints spike (27 last week vs. 12.6 avg), suggesting encampments may be contributing to resident fear
reporting_angles: Map the 18 encampment complaints from 2 weeks ago—are they concentrated in parks (Inwood Hill Park, Fort Tryon Park) or scattered?
Interview Parks Department and NYPD about enforcement activity; cross-reference with Homeless Outreach Unit sweeps or policy changes
Profile residents or service providers to understand what drove the sudden visible increase in homelessness
